questions.question: Which statement best describes a feature that shows discontinuous variation?
options: It can take any numerical value within a wide range.
It falls into specific, distinct categories with no intermediate values.
It changes constantly throughout an organism's lifetime.
It is only measured using continuous scales like length or mass.

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of continuous variation?
options: The feature can take any value within a particular range.
The feature is limited to a small number of distinct categories.
The feature is unaffected by any environmental factors.
The feature is only ever determined by a single gene.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of continuous variation in humans?
Which type of chart or graph is most suitable for displaying continuous data, such as the exact heights of students in a class?
Which of the following best explains why continuous variation is so varied in a population?
options: It is influenced by a combination of genetics, the environment, and lifestyle.
It is determined strictly by a single gene with no external influence.
It is only affected by the climate and geographical location.
It is completely random and has no genetic basis at all.

questions.question: If you are presenting data on discontinuous variation, such as human blood types, which type of graph should you use?
What is typically true about the causes of discontinuous variation?
options: It is mostly caused by the environment and changes as you age.
It usually has only a genetic cause and is not affected by environment or lifestyle.
It is highly influenced by diet, exercise, and climate.
It is caused equally by lifestyle choices and genetic factors.

questions.question: When organisms reproduce, what is the term for the biological principle that explains why a cat always gives birth to kittens and not puppies?
Why do children often look similar to their parents and siblings, showing a family resemblance?
options: Because they are exposed to different environmental factors.
Because they inherit features from both of their parents.
Because they copy the facial expressions of their parents.
Because they undergo identical mutations during growth.

questions.question: How are inherited features passed down from parents to their offspring during reproduction?
options: Through shared nutrients in the environment.
Through antibodies passed in early life.

questions.question: Which of these features is most likely to be directly caused or changed by an organism's lifestyle and environment rather than genetics alone?
options: Having a scar from a physical injury
Having a specific ABO blood group

questions.question: Why are offspring from the same parents usually not identical to their parents or to one another?
options: There is usually variation between offspring due to different combinations of inherited factors.
Parents pass on completely different sets of genes to each offspring.
Environmental factors completely erase all genetic similarities immediately.
Offspring purposely choose to develop different features to stand out.

questions.question: When comparing the features of different organisms, which of the following is true regarding differences between species?
options: Differences between species are smaller than differences within species.
Differences between species are greater than differences within species.
There are no measurable differences between organisms of different species.
Differences within a species are always exactly equal to differences between species.

questions.question: What is the scientific term used to describe the differences in the features of individuals that belong to the same species?

Which of these human features is determined entirely by inherited genetic information in the genome, without any environmental influence?
Which of the following is a feature whose variation is determined by a combination of both genetic factors and environmental/lifestyle factors?
